title: Do not negotiate on values
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What would you refuse to bargain over?

A student said that the point he took away is: you do not want to negotiate on values, which he learned from Jose early on; if you are aligned on values and they are the highest priority, then other things follow.
Jose said that when you have a partner and you have your values and integrity, you do not even need to negotiate, and it is a very powerful and lasting situation because you care about each other.

Jose said that in a negotiation he does not say: this is what I think should happen, let us break it into percentages. He says: you and I have the same values and integrity, you come up with what you think is fair for everyone.
He said that if someone walks away from a negotiation with something that disturbed them, that is not conducive to a long-term relationship.
A student said: you will always have to negotiate, and aiming for a relationship where you never need to negotiate seems wishful.
Jose said that you have to be practical in negotiation, and that he explains what is sustainable for his company, not a greedy margin, and that they want long-term client relationships.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the values you will not negotiate.
Write how you will say it.
Write your fair and sustainable number.
Write what you will do if they push on your values.
Write the long-term relationship you want.

check.q: What did a student say not to negotiate?
What does Jose ask the other side to propose?

choices: You will always have to negotiate

recap: Do not trade values. Invite a fair proposal. Be practical.
